subject: English Language
text: Neither the manager nor the workers ____ willing to change the schedule.
explanation: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearest subject; 'workers' is plural so use 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: By this time next year, I ____ my degree.
explanation: Future perfect ('will have completed') expresses an action completed before a specified future time; other forms do not show completion by then.

subject: English Language
text: He lives a very ____ life to save money.
explanation: 'Thrifty' means careful with money, matching 'to save money'. 'Lavish' and 'extravagant' are opposites; 'penurious' suggests extreme poverty.

subject: English Language
text: During the meeting, she kept a poker face.
explanation: 'Poker face' is an idiom meaning a blank or expressionless face; it does not mean anger, laughter, or questioning.

subject: English Language
text: Fix punctuation and capitals for: the president said 'we must act now,' and left.
options: The president said, "We must act now," and left.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Direct speech requires a comma before the quotation and the quoted sentence's first word capitalised; punctuation inside quotes remains with the quote.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the first syllable: teacher, control, hotel, banana?
explanation: 'Teacher' has primary stress on the first syllable (TEA-cher). 'Control', 'hotel' and 'banana' have stress on later syllables.

subject: English Language
text: Which word contains the vowel sound in 'sit' (the short /ɪ/ sound)?
explanation: 'Bit' contains the short /ɪ/ vowel as in 'sit'. 'Beam' and 'beat' have /iː/; 'bait' has the diphthong /eɪ/.

subject: English Language
text: Could you pass the salt?
explanation: Request 'Could you pass the salt?' expects an action or handing over the salt; 'Sure, here you are.' is the appropriate offering response.

subject: English Language
text: Rewrite using 'enough' without changing the meaning: He is too young to vote.
options: He is not old enough to vote.
He is not young enough to vote.
He is enough not old to vote.
He is too old to vote.
explanation: 'Too...to' converts to 'not ... enough' keeping meaning: 'He is too young to vote' = 'He is not old enough to vote.' Other options alter meaning or are ungrammatical.

subject: English Language
text: Amara locked the door after she got a phone call. She put her bag on the table and closed the curtains.
options: She wanted to invite friends in.
She planned to go out again immediately.
She was showing her bag to visitors.
explanation: Locking the door and closing curtains, plus putting her bag down, signals she wanted privacy or to be alone; inviting guests or showing a bag is inconsistent with these actions.

subject: English Language
text: Each of the books ____ damaged.
explanation: Use singular verb with 'each'; 'each of the books' requires 'is' because 'each' is singular.

subject: English Language
text: By the time the show starts, they ____ for six hours.
explanation: Future perfect continuous (will have been + -ing) expresses duration up to a future point: 'will have been practising.'

subject: English Language
text: Choose the best replacement for 'deliberate' in: 'His actions were deliberate.'
explanation: 'Deliberate' means done on purpose; 'intentional' matches this meaning, unlike 'accidental' or 'hasty.'

subject: English Language
text: If someone says 'I will bite the bullet' they mean:
explanation: Idiom 'bite the bullet' means to accept and endure something unpleasant; it implies facing difficulty bravely.

subject: English Language
text: Fix punctuation and capitals for: after the meeting john said 'we must review the plan'.
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
After the meeting John said, 'We must review the plan.'
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Capitals for proper nouns and sentence starts, comma before quotation, and capitalise inside quote: "After the meeting John said, 'We must review the plan.'".

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the first syllable: table, approve, become, inspect?
explanation: 'Ta-ble' has stress on the first syllable. 'ap-PROVE', 'be-COME' and 'in-SPECT' have main stress on the second syllable.

subject: English Language
text: Which of these words contains the same vowel sound as in 'fit'?
explanation: 'Fit' contains the short /ɪ/ vowel; 'kid' also contains /ɪ/. 'Made' /eɪ/, 'food' /uː/, 'cart' /ɑː/ differ.

subject: English Language
text: 'You might want to call ahead.' The speaker is most likely giving:
explanation: The phrasing offers a suggestion about what to do; this is characteristic of giving advice, not permission or promise.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the sentence that correctly transforms: 'Although Nia was tired, she finished the report.'
options: Being tired, Nia did not finish the report.
Nia finished the report because she was tired.
Nia finished the report despite being tired.
Since Nia was tired, she finished the report.
explanation: 'Despite being tired' preserves the contrast of 'although'. Other options reverse or change the meaning (cause or negation).

subject: English Language
text: Rita handed the keys to the new tenant and smiled. She felt content that the flat was in good hands. What does 'in good hands' mean here?
explanation: 'In good hands' is an idiom meaning cared for responsibly or well looked after; it does not mean merely locked or advertised.

subject: English Language
text: Either Lina or the coaches ____ ready for the match.
explanation: With 'either...or' the verb agrees with the nearer subject; 'coaches' is plural so use 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: By next Monday, I ____ the report.
explanation: Future perfect ('will have finished') shows an action completed before a stated future time; other forms do not express completion by that date.

subject: English Language
text: He decided to 'call it a day.' What does he mean?
explanation: 'Call it a day' is an idiom meaning to stop working or finish for the day; it does not mean delay, celebrate, or ignore.

subject: English Language
text: Fix punctuation and capitals for: 'please turn off your phones' said the lecturer.
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
"Please turn off your phones," said the lecturer.
explanation: Direct speech requires a capital at the start and a comma before the closing quote when followed by a dialogue tag: "Please...," said the lecturer.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the first syllable: hospital, control, committee, address?
explanation: HOS-pi-tal has primary stress on the first syllable; control, committee and address have primary stress on later syllables.

subject: English Language
text: Which word contains the vowel sound in 'ship'?
explanation: 'Ship' has the short /ɪ/ vowel; 'chin' also has /ɪ/. 'Cheese' = /iː/, 'chair' a diphthong, 'shoe' = /uː/.

subject: English Language
text: When Aisha arrived, the meeting ____.
explanation: Past perfect ('had started') shows the meeting began before Aisha's arrival; simple past or present perfect do not show the earlier-before-earlier relation.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the sentence that correctly begins: 'In spite of the flooded road...' from: Although the road was flooded, the bus reached on time.
options: In spite of the road flooded, the bus reached on time.
In spite of flooding the road, the bus reached on time.
In spite of that the road was flooded, the bus reached on time.
In spite of the flooded road, the bus reached on time.
explanation: 'In spite of' must be followed by a noun phrase: 'the flooded road' is correct. Other options misuse verb forms or require 'the fact that'.

subject: English Language
text: Speaker says: 'You should check the engine light.' What is the main function?
explanation: The modal 'should' expresses recommendation or advice. It is not a threat, not a direct request (no please), and not a greeting.

subject: English Language
text: Mr Bello canceled the rehearsal because the lead singer was ill. What does 'lead singer' mean?
options: the principal singer in the group
the singer who pays for the band
explanation: 'Lead singer' refers to the principal or main vocalist in a group; it does not imply paying, order of singing, or necessarily most experienced.

subject: English Language
text: Both the teacher and the students ____ excited about the trip.
explanation: A compound subject joined by and is plural and requires the plural verb 'are' for correct subject-verb agreement.

subject: English Language
text: By the time the manager arrived, they ____ for two hours.
explanation: Duration before a past reference uses past perfect continuous: 'had been waiting' shows an action continuing up to that past point.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the best replacement for 'scarce' in: 'Water became scarce during the drought.'
explanation: 'Scarce' means in short supply; 'limited' matches that sense. 'Abundant' and 'plentiful' are opposites.

subject: English Language
text: If someone says 'to bite off more than you can chew', they mean:
options: to take on more than one can handle
explanation: The idiom means to accept more responsibility or work than one can deal with; it is not about eating.

subject: English Language
text: Fix punctuation and capitals for: the headmistress announced 'school resumes monday' and smiled.
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The headmistress announced, "School resumes Monday," and smiled.
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Correct punctuation: comma before the quotation, capitalise sentence inside quotes and Monday, and include the closing comma inside the quotation marks.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the first syllable: window, agree, guitar, hotel?
explanation: Window is stressed on the first syllable (WIN-dow). Agree, guitar and hotel have stress on the second syllable.

subject: English Language
text: Which word contains the same vowel sound as in 'go' (the diphthong in 'go')?
explanation: 'Go' contains the diphthong /oʊ/ (or /əʊ/); 'coat' shares that diphthong. 'Got', 'put' and 'hot' have different vowel sounds.

subject: English Language
text: What is the main function of the sentence: 'Do you mind closing the window?'
explanation: This indirect question is a polite request form. It is not a complaint, permission question, or advice.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct passive form of: 'They had completed the survey before the meeting.'
options: The survey was completed before the meeting.
The survey had completed before the meeting.
The survey had been completed before the meeting.
The survey had been completing before the meeting.
explanation: Past perfect passive requires 'had been' + past participle: 'had been completed' accurately preserves tense and voice.

subject: English Language
text: Amid the storm, the rescue team worked tirelessly and saved every villager. What does 'tirelessly' mean here?
explanation: 'Tirelessly' means working energetically without stopping or rest; here it shows persistent, continuous effort.

subject: English Language
text: Either the coach or the players ____ the new training equipment after practice.
explanation: When subjects are joined by 'either...or', verb agrees with the nearer subject 'players' (plural), so plural 'have stored' is correct.

subject: English Language
text: By 9 o'clock tonight, Maria ____ the presentation twice to feel confident.
explanation: The future perfect 'will have practised' expresses an action completed before a specified future time; other forms do not show completion by 9 pm.

subject: English Language
text: Which option correctly punctuates and capitalises the sentence: the teacher announced 'exams start monday'
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Reported speech uses a capital for the quoted sentence and closing punctuation; standard style uses double quotes in formal writing: The teacher announced, "Exams start Monday.".

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the first syllable: mother, achieve, correct, attend?
explanation: 'mother' is stressed on the first syllable (MO-ther). 'achieve' (a-CHIEVE), 'correct' (cor-RECT) and 'attend' (at-TEND) have stress on later syllables.

subject: English Language
text: Which word contains the vowel sound in 'back' (the short /æ/ sound)?
explanation: The short /æ/ vowel appears in 'back'. 'father' has /ɑː/, 'hope' /oʊ/, and 'busy' /ɪ/ in many varieties; only 'back' matches /æ/.

subject: English Language
text: If someone says 'She threw in the towel,' they most likely mean:
explanation: 'Throw in the towel' is an idiom meaning to give up or accept defeat; literal meanings about towels or signals are not idiomatic.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the sentence that correctly transforms: 'Sam was too tired to continue.'
options: Sam was tired enough to continue.
Sam was too tired, so he continued.
Sam was so tired that he could not continue.
Sam was tired, but he continued.
explanation: 'Too...to' transforms to 'so...that' to express consequence: 'Sam was so tired that he could not continue.' Other options change the meaning.

subject: English Language
text: Complete the sentence: The committee ___ the proposal after a lengthy debate yesterday.
explanation: Context 'yesterday' signals simple past; 'accepted' is the correct past form. 'Accepts' is present, 'will accept' future, 'had accept' is ungrammatical.

subject: English Language
text: What is the main function of the sentence: 'Could you switch off the radio, please?'
explanation: 'Could you...' plus 'please' is a polite request; it is not an offer, factual information, or a direct command.

subject: English Language
text: After the flood, neighbours pulled together to clear debris. What does 'pulled together' mean here?
explanation: 'Pulled together' means to co-operate or work jointly; it implies cooperation, not arguing, separate work, or leaving.
